podcast.title: Classic Rock Covers
podcast.body: The Space Lady is known for performing covers of classic rock songs, a characteristic mentioned when introducing a sample of her music. "Susan Dietrich, otherwise known as The Space Lady, and one of her many classic rock covers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Current Status
podcast.body: As of the time of the discussion, Susan Dietrich was reportedly still residing in Colorado and was being managed by her grandson. "Last I heard, she was still in Colorado and was being managed by her grandson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career and Persona
podcast.body: Susan Dietrich, known as The Space Lady, is from Pueblo, Colorado. For many years, she was a street musician, frequently performing in cities like Boston and San Francisco. She was easily recognizable by her unique outfit: a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light. She initially played the accordion. "She wore a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light on top. And she played the accordion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Evolution
podcast.body: In the 1980s, she transitioned from playing the accordion to using a battery-powered synthesizer for her performances. "In the 80s, she moved from the accordion to a battery-powered synthesizer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Origin
podcast.body: She acquired the name "Space Lady" following some newspaper coverage of her performances. "She got the name Space Lady after some newspaper coverage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
